meta.description: Builds and applies 3D pharmacophore models using RDKit Pharm3D, the apo2ph4 receptor-based workflow, Pharmer/Pharmit for search, and PharmacoForge for protein-pocket-conditioned pharmacophore generation, covering ligand-based pharmacophores from active-set alignment and receptor-based pharmacophores from binding-pocket geometry, with explicit handling of feature types, geometric tolerances, partial matching, and pharmacophore-based virtual screening.

scientific_integrity.detail: All 5 cited DOIs (apo2ph4 10.1021/acs.jcim.2c00814, PharmacoForge 10.3389/fbinf.2025.1628800, PLIP 10.1093/nar/gkab294, Pharmit 10.1093/nar/gkw287, LigandScout 10.1021/ci049885e) verified real and correctly titled via Crossref. No fabricated statistics: all reported numbers (PLIP distances, EmbedPharmacophore embedding counts, enrichment ratios) come from real executed code on real structures.

practice_boundaries.detail: Molecular-modeling tool skill; no diagnostic/prescriptive medical conclusions in any output. Not applicable to a clinical-disclaimer requirement.

methodological_ground.detail: No principled methodological fallacy. The skill explicitly separates 'feature-type presence' from 'validated geometric bounds' and explicitly warns that its own illustrative coordinates/bounds are placeholders requiring validated derivation -- exactly the caveat that input 5's real-data test (enrichment 0.5, worse than random) shows is necessary.

code_usability.detail: Every code sample from SKILL.md ran unmodified against real installed RDKit 2026.03.6 and PLIP 3.0.1. The PLIP snippet additionally required a documented, environment-level workaround (openbabel-wheel ships no InChI writer on Windows, per TOOLS.md note 5) unrelated to the Skill's own code -- not a Skill defect, logged as a P2 documentation opportunity.

functional_suitability.note: Covers ligand-based (RDKit Pharm3D), receptor-based (apo2ph4, PLIP), pocket-conditioned generation (PharmacoForge), library search (Pharmit), and quality validation end to end; every code sample verified correct against the real installed APIs.

reliability.note: Common Errors and Per-Tool Failure Modes tables cover most failure modes with symptom/cause/fix, but the code samples themselves show no defensive handling (input3's EmbedPharmacophore call raised an uncaught ValueError on a real molecule; I had to add the try/except).

performance_context.note: SKILL.md is long (~293 lines) but well-organized into tables; usage-guide.md and one small example file keep the split reasonable.

agent_usability.note: Decision Tree by Scenario and Method Taxonomy make the right method immediately selectable; output-format guidance ('ranked hits + retrospective enrichment') is present but not detailed per scenario.

human_usability.note: Description text triggers naturally on scaffold-hopping / pharmacophore language; strict input handling is correct-by-design for this Category-3 skill, not penalized.

security.note: No credential or injection risk; the shipped example only lightly validates SMILES parse failures (if mol is None: continue).

maintainability.note: Clean 3-file split, but no dedicated test cases beyond the one demo print in examples/pharmacophore.py's __main__ block.

agent_specific.note: Well-scoped trigger with explicit Related Skills cross-references preventing overlap with scaffold-analysis/shape-similarity/virtual-screening/generative-design; SKILL.md length is just over the 500-line progressive-disclosure ideal margin is fine, minor deduction for escape-hatch phrasing not always being an explicit stop directive.

inputs.label: Receptor-based pharmacophore from a real co-crystal (PDB 1HSG, HIV-1 protease + indinavir precursor MK1) via PLIP
inputs.note: executed: true. Real PLIP 3.0.1 run on RCSB 1HSG. Correctly identified H-bonds to the catalytic Asp25/Asp25' dyad, hydrophobic contacts to the canonical S1/S1'/S2/S2' pocket residues, 2 salt bridges, and 4 water bridges -- chemically correct, matches known HIV protease inhibitor SAR. Required one documented, environment-only workaround (openbabel-wheel inchikey writer missing) unrelated to the Skill's own instructions.

assertions.note: Asp25/25' H-bonds, S1/S1'/S2/S2' hydrophobic contacts, 2 salt bridges, 4 water bridges all correctly typed by PLIP on the real structure

assertions.text: Output does not fabricate interaction records not present in the real structural geometry

inputs.label: PLIP water-bridge detection, direct contrast test of the Skill's own documented failure mode on 1HSG with/without crystallographic waters
inputs.note: executed: true. With crystallographic waters retained: 4 water bridges detected, including the physiologically critical Ile50(chain A) flap water bridging the protease flap to the ligand. With every HOH HETATM stripped from the same structure: 0 water bridges, no warning or error -- silent, exactly as SKILL.md's Per-Tool Failure Modes table describes.

assertions.text: The Skill's documented PLIP water-bridge failure mode (missing crystallographic water -> missing feature) is reproduced exactly with real structural data
assertions.note: 4 water bridges -> 0 water bridges when HOH records were stripped from the real 1HSG.pdb

assertions.text: PLIP correctly identifies the physiologically meaningful Ile50 flap water bridge when waters are retained
assertions.note: ILE50A water bridge at d(acceptor-water)=2.68/2.80 A, matching the well-documented HIV protease inhibitor flap-water interaction

assertions.text: The failure mode is silent (no error or warning raised), matching the Skill's stated symptom

key_strengths: Every code sample in SKILL.md runs exactly as documented against the real installed RDKit 2026.03.6 / PLIP 3.0.1 APIs, with zero modification required to the Skill's own logic.
All 5 literature citations (apo2ph4, PharmacoForge, PLIP, Pharmit, LigandScout) verified as real, correctly-titled DOIs via Crossref -- no fabricated references.

The Skill repeatedly and explicitly warns against treating its own illustrative bounds/coordinates as validated, and a real-data stress test (enrichment=0.5 on 5 real HIV protease inhibitors vs 5 real unrelated drugs, using the demo's literal 2-feature model) confirms exactly why that warning is necessary.

PLIP's documented water-bridge failure mode was reproduced precisely on a real co-crystal (PDB 1HSG): the physiologically important Ile50 flap-water bridge is detected with crystallographic waters present and silently vanishes when they are stripped, matching the Skill's own Per-Tool Failure Modes table.

recommendations.title: Shipped feature-family prefilter is fragile with small/diverse active sets
recommendations.problem: shared_feature_types_prefilter intersects feature-type sets across all supplied actives with no fallback; on 2 real, structurally distinct HIV protease inhibitors, the resulting common set incidentally includes 2 non-essential coincidental features that a genuine third active from the same class (ritonavir) lacks, silently rejecting it with no diagnostic of which feature was missing.
recommendations.root_cause: Strict issubset matching over a 2-active intersection, with no per-feature relaxation or scaffold-clustering step, even though the Skill's own Per-Tool Failure Modes table already documents this exact 'diverse actives confound' failure and its fix.
recommendations.fix: Have feature_family_prefilter report which query feature(s) each rejected library molecule is missing, and add a one-line pointer in its docstring to the 'cluster actives by scaffold first' fix already documented in SKILL.md's failure-mode table.

recommendations.title: Example conformer embedding has no fixed random seed
recommendations.problem: AllChem.EmbedMultipleConfs(m, numConfs=n_conf, params=AllChem.ETKDGv3()) in examples/pharmacophore.py leaves the seed unset, so repeated runs are not guaranteed to reproduce identical conformer geometries.
recommendations.root_cause: params.randomSeed is never assigned before calling EmbedMultipleConfs in the shipped example.
recommendations.fix: Set params.randomSeed to a fixed integer (matching the randomSeed=23 convention already used in SKILL.md's own EmbedPharmacophore snippet) for reproducibility.

recommendations.title: No troubleshooting note for the common openbabel-wheel InChI gap that breaks PLIP on Windows
recommendations.problem: PDBComplex.analyze() raises ValueError: inchikey is not a recognised Open Babel format on any install using the standard pip openbabel-wheel distribution, because PLIP's Ligand.__init__ unconditionally calls pybel.write(format='inchikey') and that wheel ships no InChI writer at all (a known Windows packaging gap, not something specific to this audit run).
recommendations.root_cause: SKILL.md's receptor-based PLIP snippet has no troubleshooting entry for this common environment failure.
recommendations.fix: Add a row to the Common Errors table: 'PLIP analyze() raises ValueError: inchikey is not a recognised Open Babel format | openbabel-wheel ships no InChI writer | Use a conda-forge openbabel build with InChI support, or monkeypatch pybel.Molecule.write to no-op for format="inchikey".'

recommendations.title: Worked ligand-based example has no inline warning against reuse
recommendations.problem: Plugging SKILL.md's illustrative 2-feature (aromatic+donor, 3.5-5.0 A) bounds directly into a real active/inactive HIV protease inhibitor screen gives enrichment 0.5 (worse than random), confirming the demo bounds must never be reused as-is; the prose caveat exists elsewhere in SKILL.md but the code block itself carries no inline warning.
recommendations.root_cause: The demo's query_features/bounds are placeholders by design, but nothing in the code comment signals that at the point of definition.
recommendations.fix: Add '# PLACEHOLDER COORDINATES -- do not reuse without deriving from a validated workflow' directly above the query_features block in SKILL.md's Ligand-Based Pharmacophore snippet.
